definition: The set of owners whose permission is still needed before a value, record or log line may leave or be shown to anyone new.
A decoy record planted in secret data that no legitimate output contains, so that finding it in an output is evidence of a leak.
The contract both owners sign before a sealed job starts, fixing by digest what the job may read, run and release, to whom, and within what limits.
An owner's authorized removal of their label from a value, the only way a value computed from a secret may leave the room.
A property of a randomized release: adding or removing any one record changes the probability of any set of outputs by at most a factor e^epsilon, plus a small additive slack delta.
A human that data is about: the user who typed a record, or anyone the record names.
The privacy-loss parameter of differential privacy; the factor e^epsilon bounds how much one data subject's record can change the odds of any output, so smaller is more private.
Checking a property about pairs of runs by combining two copies of a system into one and stating an ordinary invariant about the pair.
Passing a secret-derived value through an honest release so that the release carries a different piece of the secret than the contract intended.
A privacy accountant that bounds the privacy loss accumulated so far without a ceiling fixed in advance.
A privacy accountant that stops releases before a budget fixed in advance would be exceeded.
The rule that the privacy losses of successive differentially private releases add.
A bound on the total privacy loss of k releases that can be smaller than their sum, but only with a positive slack delta.
A privacy ledger that keeps one meter per data subject and charges each meter for every training round that could read that subject's records.
One customer organization served by a shared machine or harbor, such as a company, a clinic or a household, with its own agents, data and users.
Two logs that differ only in that one of them lacks every record of a single data subject.
A variant of differential privacy that bounds the Rényi divergence of a given order between a mechanism's outputs on any two neighboring inputs.
A variant of differential privacy with one parameter zeta that implies Rényi differential privacy of every order lambda with loss lambda times zeta, so costs simply add.
A small set of fine-tuned weights added to a shared model, for example one per tenant.
An attack that decides whether a given record was in a model's training data.
A tag on each log line saying who wrote it (the operator, the owner, or a third party), which decides whether other agents may read it as instructions.
Nissenbaum's account of privacy: information flows carry norms of appropriateness and distribution tied to their context, and privacy is violated when either is breached.

Said of random variables such as canary misses when any two functions of them that never decrease as one of them rises have nonnegative covariance; missing some canaries then never makes missing the others less likely.
